answer: Final best-effort pass complete; the blocked status is confirmed and final. (1) Connectivity re-tested on both http and https endpoints for rest.kegg.jp and www.genome.jp, plus raw-IP TCP (8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1) and IPv6: all fail — there is no network route at all and DNS cannot resolve, with no proxy configured. (2)–(3) Exhaustive filesystem search found NO pre-provisioned KEGG resource: no R installation or R libraries, no conda, no clusterProfiler/pathview/bioservices/gseapy caches, no .gmt/.kgml/KEGG.db/sqlite or any flat pathway-gene-set files anywhere (checked tmpfs root, the 3.5 TB /usr disk, and all NFS mounts including the runner's .actor-venv, whose site-packages contain only numpy/pandas/scipy/statsmodels/openpyxl/pip/patsy). Since no genuine KEGG pathway gene-set resource exists on disk, condition (4) does not apply and no substitute database was used, as agreed. Finalized outputs: both DESeq2 result tables extracted and validated (5,828 genes each; contrasts "Media MMGluFeMinus vs MMGluFePlus" and "Media Succinate vs MMGluFePlus"); downregulated gene sets (log2FC ≤ −1.5 AND padj ≤ 0.05): 91 genes (GluFeMinus vs GluFePlus) and 289 genes (Succinate vs GluFePlus), saved with the full tables and gene-ID lists. The approved ORA pipeline (hypergeometric + BH, universe = 5,828 tested genes restricted to KEGG-mappable genes, paer-first with pae+PA14→PAO1 fallback) is implemented and self-test-validated, and completes in one command in a networked environment: python3 analysis/kegg_ora_pipeline.py (it writes analysis/kegg_ora_result.json with the common-pathway count). The question's numeric answer (number of KEGG pathways common to both media conditions) cannot be produced here and no number is claimed.
